title: Magnetometer Calibration Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Students rotate a simulated magnetometer through a full turn and watch the raw X/Y readings trace a circle shifted away from the origin by hard-iron distortion. They compute offset = (max + min) / 2 on each axis, apply it, and see the corrected circle re-center on the origin and the compass heading error shrink.

learningObjectives: Collect magnetometer readings through a full rotation.
Compute hard-iron offsets with offset = (max + min) / 2 on each axis.
Apply the offsets to re-center the readings on the origin.
Explain how hard-iron distortion changes the compass heading from atan2(mag_y, mag_x).
standards: CCSS.MATH.CONTENT.HSG.GPE.B.6: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points (midpoint).
NGSS HS-ETS1-4: Use a computer simulation to model the impact of proposed solutions to a complex real-world problem.

controls.label: Rotate robot
controls.purpose: Adds one raw reading every 4 degrees of rotation.

controls.label: Auto-rotate
controls.purpose: Turn the robot a full 360 degrees automatically.

controls.label: Compute Calibration
controls.purpose: Enabled after a full rotation; computes the offsets, marks the center, and overlays corrected readings.

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Clear the readings and return to the default offset (35, -20).

controls.label: New robot
controls.purpose: Start over with a random hidden hard-iron offset for more practice.

equations: mag_x = 200*cos(heading) + offset_x + noise, mag_y = 200*sin(heading) + offset_y + noise
heading = atan2(mag_y, mag_x) in degrees, modulo 360
assumptions: Default hard-iron offset (35, -20) raw units, field radius 200, noise standard deviation 3.
The robot rotates flat, so only X and Y matter.
limitations: Soft-iron distortion (an oval instead of a circle) is not modeled.
Tilt compensation with the accelerometer is not modeled.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Procedure practice on a simulated sensor before doing it on hardware
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Guided four-step procedure with live min/max readouts and before/after comparison
keyQuestions: Why is the raw circle not centered on the origin?
Why does (max + min) / 2 find the center?
How much heading error does the offset cause, and at which headings?
commonMisconceptions: The magnetometer error is a single fixed angle (it depends on the heading).
Calibration only needs to be done once, forever (it must be redone after remounting the sensor).
Half a rotation is enough to find the offsets.
assessmentOpportunities: Compute offsets by hand and verify with Compute Calibration.
Record raw versus corrected heading error at four headings.
Exit ticket: compute offsets and correct a reading from given min and max values.
